body.statement: As an implementation corollary of Proposition~\ref{prop:reliability-implementation-corollary} and standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting on incidence decompositions, given \(\mathcal O_{XY}\), an exact-arithmetic input \(p\in(\mathbb Q\cap[0,1])^{E^{?}}\), and \(\mathcal T\), one can compute \(R_{XY}(p)\) and every coordinate of \(\nabla R_{XY}(p)\) exactly in \(2^{O(\tau)}\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal O_{XY}|+|E^{?}|+|\mathcal T|+B)\) bit operations, where \(B\) is the total input bit length of \(p\). A standard project--join bag state records assignments of incident uncertain-edge vertices and one witnessed-zero flag for each obstruction clause; derivatives use the conditioned evaluations \(p_e=1\) and \(p_e=0\), so the guarantee includes boundary coordinates.
body.justification: The proposition records a standard exact weighted-model-counting implementation of the newly compiled obstruction hypergraph and charges the supplied decomposition and rational bit lengths.
body.gap: Samer and Szeider supply the incidence-treewidth counting recurrence, and Dudek et al. supply literal-weighted project--join dynamic programming; this proposition claims no new generic dynamic program and only instantiates those methods after causal obstruction compilation.
body.consumer: edgeID can evaluate identification reliability and graph-refinement sensitivities whenever the emitted support hypergraph has small incidence treewidth.
